nodes.summary: A subgraph $T$ of a simple graph $G$ is a spanning tree of $G$ if it contains every vertex of $G$ and, regarded as a graph on its own vertex set, it is a tree (connected and acyclic).
nodes.title: Spanning tree

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, let $L = D - A$ be its Laplacian matrix over $\mathbb{Z}$, where $D$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$, and let $r \in V$. Then the determinant of the submatrix of $L$ obtained by deleting the row and the column of $r$ equals the number of spanning trees of $G$.
nodes.title: Matrix-tree theorem for principal minors of the Laplacian

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $r \in V$. Then the determinant of the reduced Laplacian of $G$ at $r$, that is, the integer Laplacian of $G$ with the row and the column of $r$ deleted, equals the number of spanning trees of $G$.
nodes.title: Matrix-tree theorem for a chosen root

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite nonempty vertex set $V$ and let $r \in V$. Then the determinant of the reduced Laplacian of $G$ at $r$, that is, the integer Laplacian of $G$ with the row and the column of $r$ deleted, equals the number of spanning trees of $G$.
nodes.title: Kirchhoff's matrix-tree theorem

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, the integer Laplacian of $G$ equals $D - A$, where $D$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$, both with integer entries.
nodes.title: The integer Laplacian is degree minus adjacency

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$, the integer Laplacian of $G$ is the $V \times V$ integer matrix $L$ with $L_{uu} = \deg u$ for every vertex $u$, $L_{uv} = -1$ when $u \ne v$ are adjacent, and $L_{uv} = 0$ when $u \ne v$ are not adjacent.
nodes.title: Integer Laplacian of a graph

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$, the number of spanning trees of $G$ equals the number of simple graphs $H$ on $V$ such that every edge of $H$ is an edge of $G$ and $H$ is a tree.
nodes.title: Spanning trees as trees on the whole vertex set

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, the number of spanning trees of $G$ is the number of subgraphs of $G$ that are spanning trees, that is, subgraphs that contain every vertex of $G$ and are trees.
nodes.title: Number of spanning trees

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $L = D - A$ be its Laplacian matrix over $\mathbb{Z}$, where $D$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$. For every vertex $r \in V$, the reduced Laplacian of $G$ at $r$ equals the submatrix of $L$ obtained by deleting the row and the column of $r$.
nodes.title: The reduced Laplacian is a principal submatrix

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$ and a vertex $r \in V$, the reduced Laplacian of $G$ at $r$ is the integer Laplacian of $G$ with the row and the column of $r$ deleted, a matrix indexed by the vertices of $G$ other than $r$.
nodes.title: Reduced Laplacian

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a vertex set $V$, there is an equivalence between the spanning trees of $G$ (subgraphs of $G$ that contain every vertex and are trees) and the simple graphs $H$ on $V$ that are trees with $H \le G$, that is, every edge of $H$ is an edge of $G$. It sends a spanning tree to the graph on $V$ with the same edges.
nodes.title: Spanning trees as trees contained in the graph

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
